optionReasons.saa-ini-176:option:0: The Secrets Manager invalid MFA — codes MFA are of single use and do not store.
optionReasons.saa-ini-176:option:2: Security Groups filter network TRAFFIC — they don't know if the session has MFA.
optionReasons.saa-ini-176:option:3: MFA only in the login does not prevent the use of key accesses/sessions without MFA in destructive actions — the requirement is to condition permission.

finalJustifications: Because the condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent in the policy checks if the session has been authenticated with MFA — no MFA, the destructive action is denied even with permission.
Because the condition requires a second full login to each destructive action, renewing the session before releasing the operation.
Because the condition sends a code MFA by email before executing the action, confirming the user's intention at the time.
Because the condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent only works for root user — users IAM inherit the MFA of the entire account.

finalJustifications: Because Cognito User Pools is a managed directory of end users: registration, social login and issuance of JWT (ID/access/refresh) to authorize API.
Because Cognito User Pools manages roles IAM of each app user, mapping each social login to an account identity.
Because Cognito User Pools hosts the API protected application, validating tokens without any additional gateway.
Because Cognito User Pools replaces the application backend by running the profile logic within the directory itself.

optionReasons.saa-ini-202:option:0: Individual user policies have seen a maintenance nightmare as the team grows — changes require user editing.
optionReasons.saa-ini-202:option:1: User COMPARTILHADO destroys traceability and violates basic practices — credentials never shared.
optionReasons.saa-ini-202:option:2: Access keys are for PROGRAM ACCESS — do not organize console permissions per function.

finalJustifications: Because IAM Groups by function concentrate policies: users inherit group permissions, and changing someone's function is just moving them from group.
Because IAM Groups allow shared login: members use group credentials, reducing passwords to manage.
Because IAM Groups apply MFA automatic to all members, elevating security without setting user per user.
Because IAM Groups give volume licensing discount, making scale permissions cheaper for the company.

optionReasons.saa-ini-203:option:2: IP policy is fragile (IPs change, NAT) and not authenticating the INSTANCE — is not the recommended mechanism.
optionReasons.saa-ini-203:option:3: Even in Secrets Manager, are still key accesses of LONGO PRAZO of a user IAM — the roll eliminates the need for them.

finalJustifications: Because the IAM Role via Forum Profile Delivery TEMPORARY credentials automatically rotated by IMDS — nothing static to leak or rotate by hand.
Because the Forum Profile encrypts key accesses inside the instance, protecting them even if the disk is copied.
Because the role transforms the instance into a user IAM complete, with own password rotated by AWS each session.
Because IMDS block any external access to the pocket S3, restricting calls to its bodies VPC.

optionReasons.saa-ini-205:option:0: It's wrong at the core: politics IAM DO NOT limit the root — there is no way to restrict it.
optionReasons.saa-ini-205:option:1: Any administrator IAM can create users — not exclusive root.
optionReasons.saa-ini-205:option:2: The CloudTrail REGISTRA root actions normally — audit is not the problem.

finalJustifications: Because the root has unrestricted access and executes actions that no policy IAM blocking (closing account, billing, restoring admins) — compromising it is losing the entire account.
Because root is the only user authorized to open support tickets at AWS, the recovery channel in serious account incidents.
Because the root doesn't appear in the logs of CloudTrail, and the MFA is the only compensatory control available for his administrative actions.
Because MFA in the root releases greater service limits to the account, the requirement of AWS for critical and regulated production environments.

optionReasons.saa-ini-210:option:0: Both are for consoles, CLI and SDK — the access channel is not the criterion.
optionReasons.saa-ini-210:option:1: There is no 'priority' like this: evaluation combines policies (an explicit Deny in any one win)).
optionReasons.saa-ini-210:option:3: Resource-based policies exist in several services (S3, SQS, SNS, KMS, Lambda...) — are not exclusive to S3.

finalJustifications: Because identity-based is attached to IDENTIDADE (what she can do) and resource-based to RECURSO (who can access it) — the difference is the attachment point, and the second enables cross-account access.
Because the resource-based policy also encrypts the resource in addition to controlling access — attaching it to the active bucket SSE by default on all stored objects.
Because identity-based policies can only grant Allow, and resource-based policies exist precisely for cases requiring explicit Deny over the protected resource.
Because resource-based policies are managed by AWS and automatically updated, while identity-based are the client's full responsibility.

finalJustifications: Because IAM MFA combines a virtual device (authenticator app), physical token or key FIDO2 to the user: password + code are now required in the login.
Because IAM MFA send a code by e-mail to each login attempt, validating access by the user's corporate box.
Because IAM MFA works only with token hardware sold by AWS, paired to the user at the time of purchase.
Because IAM MFA dispenses the password, using only the device's rotary code as unique access credentials.
